posts.name: Reverend Pete
posts.cooked:
Mint.

 

But it was reeeeaaal close.

 

Using Jack Handle and figuring out ways to keep it around are really helpful.

 

I used Mistbound on Baron Blade on Turn 1, so my run may be different from other people's.

 

Tantrum was a good friend, getting rid of vats I didn't want around, and freeing the team to use Cause and Effects and RPG Launchers on Villain Ongoings instead.

 

Argent Adept, Setback and Expatriette went down (Setback and Expartriette to Nightmist's last Oblivion--which also took out Friction, Blade and Proletariat). Fright Train had fallen into a Supercooled Tri-Solvent Vat a round or two earlier, so all Mr. Fixer had to do was use his Jack'ed up power on Expatriette's incap turn to take Ermine down for the win.

 

Fixer and Nightmist stood at the end, each with 2HP.

posts.name: bolnerap
posts.cooked:
Mint with Fixer at 19, Setback at 12, Nightmist at 14, Expat at 18, and PW Argent Adept at 18. And it would have been higher if Fixer hadn't punched Setback for 5 with the first hit of Crowbars to make sure they didn't get another turn.
 
This was one of the easiest Vengeance games I've ever had. Felt like the game was pitching underhanded. We won on Setback's fifth turn. Might have been able to do it a little sooner, I think going for Ermine when I did was overkill.  The KO order was Proletariat, Ermine, Friction, Fright Train, Blade.
 
- Fixer/Nightmist/Expat all did tons of AOE damage, including Expat dropping 6 on everyone but Ermine in one turn (curse you, Uncatchable)
 
- Setback/Expat/AA had multiple instances of Ongoing destruction each (and I never even saw Vernal Sonata!)
 
- AA let Fixer play a Charge off-turn to go with his Jack Handle
 
It was a slaughter. The only thing that slowed us down was Fixer getting hit with Regression Darts because he had the highest HP at the time.

posts.name: robb8888
posts.cooked:
MindWanderer:

Near Mint.  Just couldn't keep up with the destruction the first time around, and this is a setup-heavy team.  Every time I play with Dark Watch I hate them more.

+1 to that.  The DW modifications to Setback and Nightmist are almost crippling.   Most of Nightmist's impactful plays depend upon her discarding cards, and her DW version doesn't give her dependable card draw to fill her hand.   Similarly, Setback depends upon building up his unlucky pool for stuff like Turn of Events, Cash Out, and Karmic Retribution, but the DW version gets rid of a free card draw-n-play that adds tokens, and substitutes a piddly single instance of -2DR that subtracts tokens.  DW Fixer in some situations is a great teammate, but against five villains that excel in setup destruction, having a hero that destroys still more setup is ridiculous.  Expatriette – in either version – is probably my least favorite hero.  As a damage dealer, she's far less dependable than any of the other damage-dealing heroes (Ra, Haka, ChronoRanger, KNYFE), and far too prone to sitting for turn after turn with no decent guns or cards in hand, and no dependable way to draw them.
